name: Starter: Hebrew
about: Hebrew word order, gender and its little joined words in real, everyday sentences, every word with its vowels until you know it.

words.אתה: you, to a man (אַתְּ: to a woman; אַתֶּם, אַתֶּן: you all)
words.ל: to, for (לִי: to me; לְךָ: to you; לָנוּ: to us)
words.יש: there is, there are (יֵשׁ לִי: I have)
words.אין: there isn't, there aren't (אֵין לִי: I don't have)
words.כוס: glass, cup (כּוֹס מַיִם: a glass of water)
words.בית: house, home (בֵּית חוֹלִים: hospital; בֵּית סֵפֶר: school)
words.לגור: to live, in a place (גָּר, גָּרָה, גָּרִים)
words.ללכת: to go, walk (הוֹלֵךְ: goes; נֵלֵךְ: we'll go; לָלֶכֶת: to go)
words.צריך: need, have to (צְרִיכָה: said by a woman)
words.שלום: hello; peace; well-being (מָה שְׁלוֹמְךָ: how are you)
words.לקרוא: to call; to read (קוֹרְאִים לִי: my name is)
words.לאכול: to eat (אָכַלְנוּ: we ate; לֶאֱכוֹל: to eat)
words.כמה: how much, how many; a few
words.לעלות: to cost (עוֹלֶה: costs); to go up
words.תודה: thanks (תּוֹדָה רַבָּה: thank you very much)
words.לקנות: to buy (קָנִיתִי: I bought; לִקְנוֹת: to buy)
words.לנסוע: to go by car, bus or train; to travel
words.לאחר: to be late (אִיחֲרָה: she, it was late)
words.אפשר: possible; can (אֶפְשָׁר לִנְסוֹעַ: we can go)
words.לבוא: to come (בּוֹא: come!; לָבוֹא: to come)
words.עם: with (אִיתִּי: with me; אִיתָּנוּ: with us)
words.לרדת: to come down (יֵרֵד גֶּשֶׁם: it'll rain)

ma-shlomcha.about: Literally “what / your well-being,” with no word for is; to a woman it's שְׁלוֹמֵךְ, written the same.

eich-korim-lecha.about: Literally “how / people call / you”; to a woman it's לָךְ.

toda-raba.about: The Hebrew order is literally thanks much; the answer is בְּבַקָּשָׁה.

concept.line: A present-tense verb has four forms for gender and number, regardless of person: אֲנִי גָּר or גָּרָה (I live, said by a man or a woman), אֲנַחְנוּ גָּרִים, הֵן גָּרוֹת.
In simple present-tense sentences, Hebrew often leaves out English am, is and are: אָחִי סְטוּדֶנְט (my brother is a student); קַר הַיּוֹם (it's cold today).

Every noun is masculine or feminine (many feminine ones end in ה or ת), and the words with it agree: אוֹטוֹ חָדָשׁ (a new car), דִּירָה קְטַנָּה (a small apartment); Hebrew uses אַתָּה for ‘you’ when speaking to a man and אַתְּ when speaking to a woman.
A yes/no question keeps a statement's order and only the voice rises (אַתָּה מְדַבֵּר אַנְגְּלִית?); a question word like מָה, אֵיפֹה, מָתַי, אֵיךְ or כַּמָּה comes first: אֵיפֹה הַתַּחֲנָה?
לֹא (not, no) comes just before the word it denies: אֲנִי לֹא יוֹדֵעַ (I don't know); אֲנִי לֹא שׁוֹתֶה קָפֶה.

words.means: בבית = in a house; הבית = the house
התחנה = the station; תחנת = station of

concept.line: Little words take an ending for the person: לִי (to me), לָנוּ (to us), אִיתִּי (with me), שֶׁלִּי (mine), and a few nouns do too: אָחִי (my brother).

words.means: צריכה = have to; צריך = have to
